title: Mixing, editing: Cold Turkey, Don’t Worry Kyoko by Plastic Ono Band | 1971
content:
Record Plant, New York City
Producers: John Lennon, Yoko Ono, Phil Spector
Engineers: Roy Cicala, Jack Douglas

John Lennon and Yoko Ono mixed and edited two live recordings from 1969 on 2 November 1971.

The Plastic Ono Band had performed at a benefit concert on 15 December 1969 for the charity Unicef, at the Lyceum Ballroom in London. The line-up was: Lennon, George Harrison, Eric Clapton and Delaney Bramlett (guitars, with Clapton playing Rocky, Harrison’s psychedelic Fender Stratocaster); Ono (vocals); Bonnie Bramlett (tambourine); Alan White and Jim Gordon (drums); Billy Preston (organ); Klaus Voormann (bass guitar); Bobby Keys (saxophone); and Jim Price (trumpet). Lennon later referred to it as the Plastic Ono Supergroup.

They performed just two songs: the Plastic Ono Band’s current single ‘Cold Turkey’, and its b-side ‘Don’t Worry Kyoko (Mummy’s Only Looking For Her Hand In The Snow)’. The first song lasted for nearly seven minutes, and was introduced by Lennon with the words: “We’d like to do a number. This song’s about pain.”

‘Don’t Worry Kyoko’ lasted for around 40 minutes, though it was trimmed to 15 minutes for the album release. Emerick was forced to change tape reels midway through, and at least three edits are evident in the released version. It featured the guitarists and horns locked in various grooves and riffs as Ono wailed over the top.

The performance was recorded on four-track tape by Geoff Emerick, with Peter Bown and John Kurlander engineering. It was mixed two days later, and again on 31 October 1971, but evidently the results were deemed unsatisfactory, and new mixes were made on this day.

New stereo mixes of ‘Cold Turkey’ were first made, followed by new mixes and editing work on ‘Don’t Worry Kyoko’. The recordings were released on a bonus disc with the 1972 album Some Time In New York City.
